reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3, E4, E9, E10, E11) provides general support for the oxygen affinity ranking and the tendency of Mn to form porous, rapidly growing oxides, but none of the passages directly compare diffusion kinetics of Al, Si, and Mn in the equiatomic CrFeCoNiX matrix or demonstrate that slower diffusion of Al/Si leads to coherent scales in these specific alloys. The link between diffusion rates and oxide coherence is therefore assumed rather than evidenced.
premises: Al and Si have higher oxygen affinity than Mn in CrFeCoNiX alloys
Al and Si diffuse more slowly than Mn in the alloy matrix
High oxygen affinity + slow diffusion leads to coherent, dense, adherent Al2O3 or SiO2 scales
Rapid Mn diffusion + lower capacity for lattice-matched oxide leads to porous, cracked Mn-rich oxide
The oxide morphology (coherent vs. porous) directly controls protectiveness and spallation resistance
